title.value: ArguLens: Anatomy of Community Opinions On Usability Issues Using Argumentation Models
title.justification: The discussion repeatedly focuses on the framework named 'ArguLens', which is designed for analyzing usability issues in open source communities.
title.quote: We propose and evaluate ArguLens, a conceptual framework and automated technique leveraging an argumentation model to support effective understanding and consolidation of community opinions in ITSs.

analysis.description: This paper introduces ArguLens, a framework that uses an argumentation model to analyze community discussions on usability issues in open source software development. The framework is validated through content analysis and experiments with supervised machine learning to automate argument extraction. The study includes assessments on the usability of this technique by experienced users of issue tracking systems.

type.justification: The paper involves experimentation with supervised machine learning and discusses the outcomes of applying these models to argument extraction, thus making it empirical.
type.quote: We then experimented with multiple supervised classifiers using different feature sets to extract argumentative information from the discussions.

name.justification: The primary focus of this paper is on how community opinions on usability issues are structured and understood, which aligns with research in Human-Computer Interaction.
name.quote: Author Keywords: Open source software; usability; online communities; issue discussion analysis; argumentation analysis.

name.justification: The application of machine learning techniques for argument extraction from textual data indicates an emphasis on Natural Language Processing.
name.quote: Recently, Habernal et al. adapted Toulmin’s argumentation model to Web discourse. Using an annotated dataset of 340 documents, they investigated the suitability of machine learning in automated identification of argument components.

name.justification: The paper focuses on usability issues within open source software development, a specific area within software engineering.
name.quote: In open-source software (OSS), the design of usability is often influenced by the discussions among community members on platforms such as issue tracking systems (ITSs).

name.justification: The Linear SVM is identified as one of the classifiers used in the machine learning regression tasks for argument extraction in the paper.
name.quote: Specifically, we observed that both Linear Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Naive Bayes classifiers provided satisfactory results using textual features based on term frequency-inverse.

is_executed.justification: The model was applied to the dataset for argument extraction as part of the experimental validation of the ArguLens framework.

is_compared.justification: The paper compares the performance of Linear SVM with other classifiers, including Naive Bayes, Naive Bayes, and the majority-class baseline.
is_compared.quote: The best configuration for all three classification tasks was obtained using Linear SVM with TF-IDF features, achieving an average F1-score of 77.22%, 61.92%, and 61.42% for the three tasks respectively.
